correctness.rationale: The proof first establishes an exact scalar reduction for the two axis points in any absolute sum of octahedral spaces, then solves the resulting compact two-variable optimization for the cut-square norm. The upper and lower inequalities use only standard norm properties and a norming-functional consequence of octahedrality. The diagonal positive-sphere point attains both scalar bounds simultaneously, so no optimization gap remains. Exact-rational boundary checks independently replay the closed form on finite grids.
risks: The claim is restricted to the two-axis simultaneous witness constant and does not identify other quantitative octahedrality moduli.

value.rationale: The finding quantitatively refines a standard qualitative preservation criterion on a natural nested interpolation between the two classical absolute norms that do preserve octahedrality. It gives a reusable scalar reduction and exposes a sharp non-monotone interior obstruction with an exact worst parameter and value, so it is a motivated structural calculation rather than an arbitrary slice or table lookup.
risks: The invariant addresses a distinguished two-point test rather than every quantitative notion of octahedrality.
